title: Perform Humane Pork Slaughtering Procedures in an Abattoir

lessons.title: Receiving and handling pigs humanely
lessons.html:
Why humane handling matters

Pigs feel pain and fear. The Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962 makes it an offence to treat animals cruelly, and the meat safety rules require humane handling at the abattoir. Calm pigs are also safer to work with and give better meat. Stressed pigs can give pale, soft, watery pork, and rough handling causes bruises that must be trimmed off.

Off-loading and the lairage

  1. Check the truck when it arrives. Look for dead, injured, or very weak pigs and report them to the supervisor and the meat inspector at once.
  2. Off-load quietly using the ramp. Let pigs walk at their own speed.
  3. Put pigs into lairage pens without overcrowding. Keep pigs from different farms apart if your plant procedure says so, because unfamiliar pigs fight.
  4. Make sure there is clean drinking water in every pen.
  5. The meat inspector does the ante-mortem inspection (inspection before slaughter). Sick or suspect pigs are kept apart as instructed.

Moving pigs

  • Pigs move best in small groups. Use a pig board (a solid board) to guide them.
  • Pigs follow other pigs and move from dark to light. Remove things that frighten them: shadows, hanging chains, loud noises, water puddles that shine.
  • Use your voice softly. Do not shout.

Never

  • Never kick, hit or beat a pig, or lift it by the ears, tail or legs.
  • Never use sharp sticks or pipes.
  • Do not use an electric prodder on pigs unless your plant procedure allows it for a pig that refuses to move, and never on the face, eyes, anus or belly.

lessons.title: Stunning
lessons.html:
The purpose of stunning

Stunning makes the pig unconscious so that it feels no pain when it is stuck and bled. The pig must stay unconscious until it dies from loss of blood. Only trained and authorised workers may stun.

Stunning methods for pigs

  • Electrical stunning: tongs are placed on the head, on both sides behind the ears, so current passes through the brain. Some plants also apply current across the heart.
  • Gas stunning: in larger plants, pigs are lowered in groups into a pit with a high concentration of carbon dioxide.
  • Captive bolt: used mainly for emergencies or very large boars.

The equipment settings, such as the current and the time the tongs are held on, are set by the plant. Follow your abattoir's procedure and do not change settings.

Doing electrical stunning well

  1. Check the stunner before the shift: cables, tongs, display, and that it works on the test unit if your plant has one.
  2. Restrain the pig calmly in the stunning pen or restrainer.
  3. Place the tongs firmly in the right position. Wet, clean tongs make better contact.
  4. Hold for the full time your procedure says.

Signs of an effective stun

  • The pig collapses at once and goes stiff, then may kick.
  • No normal rhythmic breathing.
  • No blinking when the eye is touched (no corneal reflex).
  • No attempt to lift the head or call.

If you see any sign of the pig waking, stun again immediately and tell the supervisor. Never stick a pig that is not properly stunned.

Safety

Wear rubber boots and dry gloves. Never touch the tongs while switched on. Report damaged cables.

lessons.title: Shackling, sticking and bleeding
lessons.html:
Shackling

After stunning, the pig is shackled by one hind leg and hoisted onto the bleeding rail, or bled lying on a table, as your plant does it. Work fast: the time from stunning to sticking must be short, so the pig cannot wake up. Your abattoir sets this time; follow it.

Sticking

Sticking means cutting the large blood vessels near the heart so that blood drains out quickly.

  1. Use a clean, sharp, sterilised sticking knife.
  2. Make the cut in the middle of the neck, in front of the breastbone, as you were trained.
  3. Point the knife towards the heart and cut the main vessels. Do not push the knife into the chest too deep, because this lets blood into the chest cavity.
  4. Withdraw the knife and put it in the sterilizer before the next pig. Many plants use two knives in turn so one is always in the sterilizer.

Bleeding

Let the pig bleed for the full time your procedure requires before scalding. A pig that is not fully bled out gives poor meat and must never go into the scald tank alive. Check that the pig shows no signs of life before scalding.

  • Blood is collected in the bleeding trough. If blood is collected for use, follow the plant's hygiene rules.
  • Keep the bleeding area clean and the floor free of slippery blood.

Safety at sticking

  • Stunned pigs kick hard. Stand to the side, never directly behind the legs.
  • Wear a chain-mail apron and cut-resistant glove if provided.
  • Always cut away from your body and hands.

Key points

  • Handle pigs calmly; never hit, kick or lift them by the ears or tail.
  • Report dead, injured or sick pigs to the supervisor and meat inspector.
  • Check every pig for signs of an effective stun; re-stun at once if it is not.
  • Stick quickly after stunning with a sterilised knife.
  • Never scald a pig that shows signs of life.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of stunning a pig?

options.text: To make it unconscious so it feels no pain during sticking and bleeding

quiz.question: Which is a sign of an effective stun?

options.text: The pig blinks when the eye is touched
The pig breathes normally and tries to lift its head
The pig collapses at once and has no corneal reflex

quiz.question: A stunned pig starts to breathe normally and lift its head. What do you do?

options.text: Wait for it to calm down
Put it back in the pen
Stun it again immediately and tell the supervisor

quiz.question: What is the best tool for guiding pigs in the lairage?
Why should the sticking knife go into the sterilizer between pigs?

options.text: To keep it warm for the worker
To kill germs so they are not carried into the next carcass
Because the meat inspector likes it

quiz.question: Pigs move more easily from dark areas into lighter areas.
Workers may change the stunner settings if they think it will speed up the line.
Which actions are cruel and not allowed when handling pigs? (select all that apply)

options.text: Lifting a pig by its ears or tail
Kicking a pig that will not move
Using the electric prodder on the pig's face
